Order 
This is an appeal filed by the Insurance Company u/S 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being aggrieved by the award dated 05.12.2024 passed by IInd Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Dabra, District Gwalior [in short "Claims Tribunal"] in MACC No.03/2023 seeking reduction of compensation amount on the ground that Claims Tribunal has committed an error in deducting income towards personal expenses 1/3 instead of 1/2.
2.
The date of accident and negligence are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

3. As per the findings of the Tribunal, in the case of death of Anuj Sahu, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.18,45,600 along with interest from the date of application till realization.

4. Learned counsel for Insurance Company submitted that Claims Tribunal NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:16584 2 MA-2767-2025 has committed an error in deducting income towards personal expenses 1/3 instead of 1/2.

It is further contended that deceased was bachelor,
therefore, considering the fact that deceased is bachelor, his dependency ought not to be more than 50 per cent only for respondent No.2 i.e. mother of deceased and Claims Tribunal has also The New India Assurance Co Ltd vs Kallu @ Vinod Sahu

Therefore, it is prayed that dependency must be reduced to the extent of 1/2 instead of 1/3.
5.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents contended that the amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal is just and proper and needs no reduction.
He supported the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

6. After hearing learned counsel for both the parties and on perusal of the record, it is undisputed fact that deceased was bachelor and there is no evidence adduced by respondents/claimants that other respondents are dependent upon the income of the deceased.
7.
So, in the considered opinion of this Court, Claims Tribunal has committed an error in deducting dependency to the extent of 1/3 instead of 1/2 in favour of respondents.
The finding of the tribunal in this regard is not correct in the eye of law and is hereby set aside.
Thus, the compensation awarded by the tribunal is modified as under:
HEAD AMOUNT  Income Rs.8500 per month x 12= Rs. 1
Future prospects (40%) Rs.40800/-

 --------------
TOTAL Rs.14,
8 . Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.14,17,200/- as against the award the award of the Tribunal o f Rs.18,45,600/-.
Accordingly, the compensation amount is reduced from Rs.18,45,600/- to Rs.14,17,200/-.
9. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed by reducing the compensation amount to a sum of Rs.14,17,200/-.
The said amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Claims Tribunal from the date of the filing of the claim petition till its realization.
